A framework for asking research questions

All three points in the drawing are allowed. At first, the available steps connect A to B, but not B to C. Add the missing step and C becomes reachable from A.

The wider research makes this distinction carefully: being allowed, staying within the rules over time, and being reachable are different requirements. Drawing a desirable destination does not build the bridge.

Add the missing step. See which point you can reach from A.

Words used here
admissibility
Whether something meets the stated rules or constraints. It does not mean that it will happen or that we can reach it.
Read the fuller explanation

In the investigation framework, possibility, admissibility, viability and reachability are different regions. A state may satisfy the static constraints while no available sequence of controls can reach it from your starting point.

A viable history must also remain within its conditions for the required duration. A beautiful endpoint drawn beyond a broken bridge does not supply the missing construction. Declaring a desired optimum cannot replace that bridge.

The distinction travels usefully into making things. Name the start, the available actions, the constraints along the way and the evidence of arrival. That is an editorial use of the framework, not a proof that physical and human choices share one dynamics.
